rv.q: Perhaps even more surprising is that, somehow, they pull it off.
There’s only so much you can “elevate” about a work that fundamentally wants to revel in some schlocky mud.
Masquerade is a lot of fun if you're in the right mood.
This entire revitalized gothic romance with its 1980s guitar riffs has that invigorating effect.
You can either stage “Phantom” in a theater or create a non-narrative funhouse party experience, but trying to do both at once satisfies neither.

The result of this world creation is a truly moving, unforgettable experience that takes you to the darkest depths of the human mind; yet it still provides hope for a brighter future filled with music and light.
Paulus and team have pulled off something miraculous: an immersive evening that retains the essence and dramatic arc of its source material.
